q: An employee walks up to a shared kiosk and types her username; the system then prompts for her password and a one-time code from her phone before displaying her records. Typing the username is an example of which security process?
c: Identification
Authentication
Authorization
Accountability

q: A newly hired CISO at a logistics company is asked to build the organization's first formal security program. Several managers are pushing for an immediate purchase of endpoint detection tooling to show progress. What should the CISO do FIRST?
c: Approve the endpoint tooling purchase to deliver a quick win and build political capital with the managers
Commission an external penetration test to identify the most exploitable technical weaknesses
Review the organization's mission, business objectives, and regulatory obligations so the security strategy is aligned with them
Draft a complete set of security policies by adopting an industry framework's template library wholesale

q: A bank structures its risk program on the three-lines-of-defense model. Operational teams own and manage risk daily, and a central risk management function sets policy and monitors compliance. The board asks which function should periodically provide independent assurance that the first two lines are actually effective. What is the appropriate answer?
c: The enterprise risk management office, since it already monitors control compliance across the organization
The CISO's security operations team, because it has the deepest technical insight into control performance
The banking regulator, because true independence requires assurance from a body outside the organization
Internal audit, reporting to the board or its audit committee, acting as the third line of defense

q: A European airline collected passport details from passengers solely to satisfy government immigration requirements. Its marketing department later proposes mining those same records to build nationality-based advertising segments without informing passengers. Which privacy principle does this proposal MOST directly violate?
c: Data minimization, because the airline gathered more personal data than its operations actually required
Purpose limitation, because data collected for one declared purpose is being repurposed for an incompatible use without notice or a lawful basis
Data localization, because the passport records would be moved between departments in different countries
Storage limitation, because the airline has clearly retained the passport records for longer than necessary

q: A national health regulator, acting under authority delegated to it by the legislature, issues detailed security rules that hospitals must follow and can levy monetary penalties for noncompliance through its own enforcement proceedings rather than a court trial. Which category of law do these rules represent?
c: Administrative law, because they are regulations promulgated and enforced by a government agency under delegated authority
Criminal law, because monetary penalties can be imposed on hospitals that fail to comply with the rules
Civil law, because disputes about the rules would ultimately be resolved between private parties seeking damages
Contract law, because hospitals implicitly agree to the rules as a condition of operating in the sector

q: During an internal investigation into missing warehouse inventory, an investigator meets with an employee who is not suspected of wrongdoing to learn what she observed during her night shifts. What is this information-gathering session properly called?
c: An interrogation
A deposition
An interview
Surveillance

q: In a civil trial, opposing counsel moves to exclude a company's authentication logs, arguing they are inadmissible hearsay because no human witnessed the events the logs record. Which response BEST explains why the logs can nevertheless be admitted?
c: System logs are direct evidence of the events they capture and therefore can never be subject to a hearsay objection in any court
Records generated automatically in the ordinary course of business are admissible under the business records exception when the organization can show they were created and preserved reliably
Digital evidence is exempt from ordinary admissibility rules whenever a completed chain of custody form accompanies it into the courtroom
The best evidence rule obligates the court to accept the logs because the company produced the original files rather than copies

q: A security team wrote a comprehensive information security policy, published it on the intranet, and covered it in annual training. Yet several department heads refuse to fund the controls it requires, dismissing it as 'the security team's wish list.' What is the MOST likely root cause of this situation?
c: The policy is too long and detailed and needs to be decomposed into separate standards and procedures
The policy lacks sufficient technical specifics, so department managers cannot determine what they must implement
Employees have not individually signed acknowledgment forms confirming they have read and understood the policy
The policy was never formally approved and issued by senior management, so it carries no organizational authority over the departments

q: An internal audit finds that 70 percent of engineering staff routinely use an unapproved file-transfer tool because the approved method cannot handle the file sizes their work requires. Line managers have tolerated the practice for over a year. What is the BEST course of action for the security manager?
c: Re-evaluate the policy and approved tooling with business stakeholders and update them so a sanctioned method meets the legitimate operational need
Begin formal disciplinary proceedings against all violating engineers to re-establish the policy's credibility and deterrent effect
Grant a permanent enterprise-wide exception allowing the unapproved tool so that current practice and policy are aligned
Reclassify the file-transfer policy as a guideline so that using the alternative tool is no longer a reportable violation

q: A manufacturer's leadership believes continuity planning is complete because IT maintains a tested disaster recovery plan that restores all servers within agreed RTOs at a secondary data center. A consultant reviewing the overall program disagrees. What critical gap is the consultant MOST likely to identify?
c: The secondary data center should be upgraded to a fully mirrored hot site to eliminate any restoration delay for the servers
The recovery time objectives are unreliable because they were never benchmarked against published industry averages for manufacturers
Restoring IT systems covers only part of continuity; the program lacks plans for people, facilities, suppliers, and manual business processes during a disruption
The disaster recovery plan should be merged with the incident response plan into a single consolidated document for consistency

q: A regional insurer's continuity plans all assume the primary facility becomes unavailable while staff remain able to work. During a severe influenza season, 40 percent of the claims department is absent for three weeks and the plans provide no help, even though every system and building operates normally. Which improvement should the BCP coordinator prioritize?
c: Procure a mobile recovery trailer so that claims staff can relocate quickly whenever the primary facility becomes unusable
Extend the plan's scenario coverage to loss of personnel, adding cross-training, succession planning, and remote or surge staffing strategies
Shorten the claims systems' recovery time objectives so that processing can resume more quickly after any future outage event
Purchase business interruption insurance sized to compensate the company for revenue lost during the seasonal slowdown

q: A quarterly access review finds dozens of active network accounts belonging to contractors whose engagements ended months earlier. Sponsoring managers admit they rarely remember to request deactivation when contracts close. Which control BEST prevents this condition from recurring?
c: Require all contractors to sign strengthened nondisclosure agreements before any account is issued to them
Increase the access review cadence from quarterly to monthly so stale contractor accounts are discovered sooner
Route every contractor login through the corporate VPN with multifactor authentication for stronger identity assurance
Provision contractor accounts with automatic expiration dates tied to the contract end date, requiring sponsor action to renew

q: A director asks HR to skip the standard pre-employment background check for a personal friend he is hiring into a role that approves customer refunds, saying he can 'personally vouch' for the candidate's character. What should HR do?
c: Apply the standard screening required for the role's sensitivity, regardless of the personal referral
Waive the background check but schedule more frequent performance reviews during the probationary period
Accept the director's personal vouching as a documented compensating control equivalent to screening
Onboard the candidate immediately and complete the background check at some point during the first year

q: A finance team reconciles payment-system transaction logs against bank statements every week specifically to discover any unauthorized transfers that have already occurred. Which control type does this reconciliation represent?
c: Preventive control
Deterrent control
Detective control
Corrective control

q: Three years ago management formally accepted the risk of running a customer portal without web application firewall protection because attack activity was minimal. Since then the portal's user base has grown tenfold and automated attacks against similar portals have surged. What does this situation BEST illustrate?
c: Risk acceptance is permanent once documented, so no action is required unless an actual incident occurs on the portal
Accepted risks must be revisited on a defined schedule or when conditions materially change, because the original decision may no longer be valid
The original acceptance was invalid from the start, because acceptance is never an appropriate response for internet-facing systems
The risk has effectively transferred to the portal's users, since they are the ones who benefit from the service it provides

q: A federal agency completes control implementation and independent assessment for a new case-management system, and the assessment report documents several residual risks. Before the system may operate in production, who must formally decide the residual risk is acceptable, and what is that decision called?
c: The information system security officer signs the system security plan, which constitutes the system's formal accreditation decision
The independent control assessor issues a certification statement, which also serves as the final approval for the system to begin operating
The system administrator records management's acceptance in the risk register on behalf of the organization before the system goes live
A senior authorizing official reviews the residual risk and grants an authorization to operate, formally accepting the risk on the organization's behalf

q: A CISO wants a risk-focused evaluation driven by the organization's own business and operational staff through facilitated workshops, cataloging critical assets, the threats to them, and current protection practices across the whole enterprise, rather than a developer-led analysis of a single application's design. Which methodology BEST matches this description?
c: OCTAVE
PASTA
STRIDE
DREAD

q: During requirements definition for a new payments feature, a business analyst documents scenarios describing how a hostile actor might deliberately exploit each planned function, such as replaying a captured transfer request, so security requirements can be written alongside the functional ones. Which technique is being applied?
c: Regression testing of the payment feature
Fuzz testing of the payment interfaces
Red team exercises against the environment
Misuse and abuse case modeling

q: A telecom operator orders routers from an overseas factory and is concerned that firmware or components could be altered while shipments sit in intermediate warehouses along the logistics route. Which combination of measures BEST addresses tampering during transit?
c: Require the freight carrier to provide continuous GPS tracking and location history for every shipment in the supply chain
Use tamper-evident packaging with serialized seals and validate delivered firmware against vendor-published cryptographic hashes before deployment
Purchase transit insurance covering the full replacement value of each router shipment moving through the intermediate warehouses
Run a standard vulnerability scan against each router once it has been installed and placed into production service

q: After a managed service provider was breached, attackers used its always-on administrative VPN tunnels to reach dozens of the MSP's customers. Your company's systems were not accessed, and management wants to retain the MSP. Which change MOST reduces the risk of a repeat scenario harming your organization?
c: Add a contract clause requiring the MSP to notify your company of any security breach within 24 hours of discovery
Require the MSP to carry substantially higher cyber liability insurance naming your company as an additional insured party
Replace standing connectivity with just-in-time, MFA-protected access through a monitored gateway restricted to the specific systems the MSP manages
Request the MSP's most recent SOC 2 Type II report each year and review it carefully for control exceptions

q: Completion rates for annual security awareness training are 99 percent, but interviews reveal most staff click through the modules without reading, and behavioral metrics have not improved in two years. The training content itself is accurate and current. What change would BEST improve the program?
c: Make the modules longer and more technically detailed so that employees are compelled to take the material seriously
Tie module completion to payroll release so that no employee can possibly skip the required annual training
Replace the interactive modules with a signed annual acknowledgment that each employee has read the security policy
Redesign delivery around engagement, using short interactive scenarios and gamified challenges with recognition, and measure behavior change instead of completion

q: During a routine malware investigation on a marketing employee's workstation, a security analyst discovers files that appear to be illegal child sexual abuse material, unrelated to the original incident. What should the analyst do FIRST?
c: Create a working copy of the suspicious files on encrypted media so the evidence is documented before it can be deleted
Complete the malware investigation as originally scoped and note the discovery in the final report for management review
Stop examining the system, preserve it in its current state, and escalate through management and legal counsel so law enforcement can be engaged
Notify human resources so the employee can be suspended and interviewed about the material

q: A courier loses a box of unencrypted backup tapes containing customer account records while transporting them to an offsite vault. The tapes are never recovered. Which security principle has MOST directly been violated?
c: Confidentiality, because customer data may now be read by unauthorized parties
Integrity, because the organization can no longer verify that the records remained accurate
Availability, because the tapes can no longer be used to restore the customer data
Nonrepudiation, because the courier can now deny responsibility for losing the shipment

q: A mid-sized manufacturer wants a voluntary, flexible framework that gives executives and business partners a common language for describing its current cybersecurity posture and its improvement targets. Certification is not a goal. Which option BEST fits this need?
c: ISO/IEC 27001, with a certification-scoped management system audit
The NIST Cybersecurity Framework, mapped to current and target profiles
PCI DSS, applied across all business processes rather than card data alone
COBIT, used to define enterprise IT governance and management objectives

q: Investigators trace the theft of a company's trade secrets to an individual operating from a country that has no extradition treaty with the company's home nation. Executives insist the person be prosecuted. Which response reflects the MOST realistic understanding of the legal situation?
c: File a civil suit in the company's home courts, which will compel the foreign government to surrender the suspect
Contact the foreign country's police directly and request an immediate arrest based on the company's forensic evidence
Ask Interpol to issue an international arrest warrant so the suspect can be detained in any member country
Refer the case to domestic law enforcement, recognizing that mutual legal assistance channels and jurisdictional limits will shape what is possible

q: Immediately after a significant breach is confirmed, the general counsel of a company facing likely litigation instructs that the external forensic firm be retained by outside counsel rather than contracted directly by the IT department. What is the PRIMARY reason for structuring the engagement this way?
c: It guarantees the forensic examiners remain independent of the IT staff whose systems failed
It positions the investigation under legal privilege so its findings are prepared in anticipation of litigation
It ensures chain of custody is preserved because attorneys are trained in evidence handling
It transfers legal liability for the breach from the company to the outside law firm

q: A severe storm floods part of a company's primary data center. For six hours, department heads debate by phone whether the situation is bad enough to invoke the business continuity plan, while recovery windows slip away. Which improvement would BEST prevent this delay from recurring?
c: Define objective activation criteria in the plan and designate specific roles with authority to declare a disaster
Lengthen the recovery time objectives so the plan can absorb several hours of executive deliberation
Schedule more frequent full-interruption exercises so leadership becomes comfortable invoking the plan
Delegate the invocation decision to the on-call facilities engineer who first observes the damage

q: A line manager reports that a systems engineer who was passed over for promotion has become withdrawn, has begun copying unusually large volumes of project files, and recently mentioned interviewing with a direct competitor. What is the MOST appropriate way for the security function to proceed?
c: Have the manager quietly restrict the engineer's access and personally review the engineer's email
Engage the established insider-threat process so HR, legal, and security can review the indicators and coordinate a proportionate response
Terminate the engineer immediately and revoke all access before any project data leaves the organization
Wait until data loss is confirmed by monitoring alerts so any action taken rests on conclusive technical evidence

q: A newly hired risk executive must build an enterprise risk management program from the ground up. Before any risks are assessed or safeguards are chosen, which activity should be completed FIRST?
c: Conduct a quantitative assessment of the organization's highest-value information assets
Select and implement a baseline of controls mapped to a recognized control framework
Deploy dashboards that track key risk indicators across all business units
Establish the risk frame, documenting assumptions, constraints, priorities, and the organization's risk appetite

q: A threat intelligence team wants to model targeted intrusions as an ordered sequence of adversary stages, from reconnaissance and weaponization through delivery, exploitation, and actions on objectives, so defenders can design controls that break the sequence as early as possible. Which model matches this description?
c: The Cyber Kill Chain, developed by Lockheed Martin
The MITRE ATT&CK knowledge base of adversary tactics
The STRIDE threat categorization scheme
The Diamond Model of Intrusion Analysis

q: A hospital's patient-scheduling operations depend entirely on a single SaaS provider. During contract renewal, the CISO notes that the agreement says nothing about what happens if the hospital ever needs to leave the platform. Which contract addition BEST reduces this supply chain risk?
c: A source code escrow arrangement that releases the application code if the vendor becomes insolvent
Stronger service-level penalties and availability credits for unplanned platform downtime
Termination assistance and data portability clauses requiring export of the hospital's records in documented, open formats
A right-to-audit clause allowing annual review of the vendor's security control environment
